title: Sentinel Shield accepted risks (schema v2)
description: Accepted risks are EXECUTABLE POLICY: each record can stop a gate from failing. v2 closes every object (additionalProperties:false) because an ignored unknown field is dangerous — a field meant to NARROW an exception (a misspelled `components`, say) that is silently dropped BROADENS the suppression. Deliberate additions live in `extensions` and are informational only. v2 also requires the authorisation dates the 90/30/365 validity policy needs.

version.description: Schema version. Exactly "2"; consumers fail closed on anything else. Legacy "1"/"1.1" files are read only under the documented migration policy and are refused by strict/regulated.

generated_at.description: Optional provenance stamp written by the migration tool.

migrated_from.description: Written by `migrate-accepted-risks.sh`. Records what this file was produced from; never hand-authored.

source_version.description: The schema version of the legacy input.

migrated_at.description: UTC timestamp of the migration run.

source_digest.description: SHA-256 of the legacy input, so the migration can be traced to exact bytes.

risks.description: Every accepted risk. Ids must be unique; duplicates fail closed.

id.description: Stable unique identity. Reported wherever the record suppresses something, so an audit can name the approval.

gate.description: The gate this record may suppress. Must be one the engine declares suppressible; a never-suppressible gate fails closed.

scope.description: `finding` (default, narrow) or `gate` (broad, loudly reported). No other value is a scope.

status.description: Lifecycle status. Only `approved` suppresses anything. Unknown statuses fail closed.

owner.description: Accountable owner for remediating the underlying risk.

reason.description: Why the risk is accepted. An empty justification is not a justification.

mitigation.description: Compensating control in place while the risk is accepted.

created_at.description: Real calendar date (UTC) the record was authored.

approved_at.description: Real calendar date (UTC) the exception was AUTHORISED. The validity window is measured from here; a future date fails closed. Required for approved records and, once #227 lands, must match the verified approval attestation.

expires_at.description: Real calendar date (UTC) the acceptance ends. The EFFECTIVE expiry is the earliest of this date, the configured tightening, the mode limit and the absolute ceiling.

approval.description: Who authorised this record and under what authority. Editable strings here are CLAIMS; #227 replaces them with a verified platform attestation.

approved_by.description: Approver identity. Must differ from `owner` — separation of duties.

authority.description: The policy, team or role under which the approval was given.

reference.description: Immutable reference for the approval (PR, review or ticket URL).

scanner.description: Producer whose findings this record may match.

rule_ids.description: Rule identifiers to match. Every member must be a non-empty string.

files.description: Repository-relative paths. Absolute paths, traversal, globs and control characters are refused; matching is exact.

issue.description: Tracking issue or ticket for remediation.

incident.description: Incident reference, when the acceptance came from one.

emergency.description: True when accepted under an emergency process. Informational: it never widens what the record matches.

supersedes.description: Id of the older record this one replaces. Renewal creates a NEW record; it never edits the original expiry.

extensions.description: The ONLY place consumer or vendor metadata may live. Keys are namespaced `vendor.example/key`. Extension data is informational: it never alters matching, suppression, status, expiry, approval or gate behaviour.

then.description: An APPROVED record must say when it was authorised: the validity window is measured from approved_at.
